case.title: A card's More actions menu appears on hover or focus and offers Reassign
case.custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role, which has Work orders > View and Create & Edit) at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Technician {Technician-A} is active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and is pinned in your Board View.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C96945 Ana.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has one Approved work order, {Work-order-1}, led by {Technician-A}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C96945 Card Menu and {Work-order-1} is S10043-17731.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
case.custom_steps:
1. Hover the card for {Work-order-1}.
  2. Click the "More actions" (…) button that appears.
  3. Read the menu items.
  4. Press Escape.
  5. Move the mouse off the card.
  6. Click once in the "Search" box.
  7. Press Tab until a card shows a focus ring.
  8. Use the arrow keys to move the focus ring to the card for {Work-order-1}.
case.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the "More actions" (…) button appears on the card.
  • Step 2: the card's menu opens.
  • Step 3: the menu includes "Reassign lead technician".
  • Step 4: the menu closes.
  • Step 5: the "More actions" button is hidden again.
  • Step 6: the cursor is in the "Search" box.
  • Step 7: a card shows the focus ring.
  • Step 8: the card for {Work-order-1} shows the focus ring and its "More actions" (…) button shows without hovering.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10046 (Story 3, Board View — board by lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 61 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S3-R13, S3-R14, S11-R1 and S11-R3, read 16 Oct 2026. Design: Claude Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Work Orders.dc.html), Board card more-actions menu; on-screen labels only. Source-verified 16 October 2026. Last checked against build v26.40.19-1493c63 (staging) on 10/16/2026.

Until 16 Oct 2026 this case reached the card by pressing Tab repeatedly. PRD version 54 said Tab reaches every row, card and header in on-screen order. PRD versions 55, 60 and 61 (15 and 16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward rulings on Slavcho Mitrov's questions and the QA triage of SV-11395, SV-11397, SV-11422 and SV-11421) changed this: each view is one Tab stop that lands on a work order, and the arrow keys move between cards, rows, headers and columns. This case follows version 61, the latest.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R13: “Reveal the card’s more-actions overlay on hover or keyboard focus.”
  • S3-R14: “Include Reassign lead technician in the card’s more-actions menu.”
  • S11-R1: “Each view is a single Tab stop. Tab lands on one work order row (Tech View) or card (Board View), the one last focused, or the first one when none has been (never a group or column header while a work order is shown; when every group is collapsed, Tab lands on the first group header; after the user arrows onto a header and tabs out and back in, Tab returns to a work order row while any row is shown; on Board View, if the last-focused card has scrolled out of view in its column, Tab lands on the first card in view); the focused row or card shows a visible focus ring.”
  • S11-R3: “Inside a view the arrow keys move focus: Up and Down move between rows and group headers in Tech View, and between cards and the column header within a Board View column; Left and Right move between Board View columns. Tab from a focused row, card or header reaches its own controls (more actions, pin, collapse) in order, then leaves the view. Tab never stops on every row.”

changes.new_value:
1. Sign in to the build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit (check in Settings > Roles & Permissions > open your role > Work Orders section). The Admin role has both.
  2. Use a desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  3. In the top bar, choose the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Create everything below in this location.
  4. Make sure the location has the technicians this case uses (e.g. "Esther Howard"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff record is Active, Clockable is on, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member > enter the first and last name (e.g. Esther Howard), role Technician, Clockable on, Active, enrolled at this location > Save.
  5. Create the work orders this case uses and set their lead technician (e.g. S1-702 led by Esther Howard):
    • Work Orders > New Work Order > choose a customer (e.g. "Fibridge Commercial") and an asset (e.g. unit TRK-118, 2022 Freightliner M2) > Create. Write down the number the build gives the work order (the numbers in this case are examples).
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician (e.g. Esther Howard) and save. Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.

changes.label: Steps
changes.old_value:
1. Switch to Board View.
  2. Hover a card (and move keyboard focus to it).
  3. Confirm the more-actions control appears.
  4. Open it and confirm it lists Reassign lead technician.
changes.new_value:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab on the left of the toolbar.
  3. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Board View (in the design its tooltip reads "Board").
  4. Hover the S1-702 card.
  5. Click the more-actions button (three dots) that appears.
  6. Read the menu items.
  7. Press Escape and move the mouse off the card.
  8. Press Tab repeatedly until the S1-702 card (or a control inside it) has keyboard focus.

changes.new_value:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 10 minutes
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011). A desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  • [User-A]: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • One technician at this location: [Tech-A] (e.g. "Esther Howard"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Card Menu" (used by this case only), with one contact and one asset, so this case's work orders are kept apart from every other work order at the location.
  • One Approved work order for that customer, [WO-1], led by [Tech-A].
  • Names and numbers are examples.

Setup

  1. Sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page (you appear as "Admin ShopView"). Check the location in the top bar next to the bell; to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  2. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: confirm each technician below is active at this location with Time Clock on, or add it: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] (e.g. Esther Howard).
  3. Top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Card Menu" > Save (if it already exists, open it instead). On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, TRK-118) > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  4. Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Card Menu" and its asset > Save. Design: Claude Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Work Orders.dc.html), Board card more-actions menu; on-screen labels only. Source-verified 16 October 2026. Until 16 Oct 2026 this case reached the card by pressing Tab repeatedly. PRD version 54 said Tab reaches every row, card and header in on-screen order. PRD versions 55, 60 and 61 (15 and 16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward rulings on Slavcho Mitrov's questions and the QA triage of SV-11395, SV-11397, SV-11422 and SV-11421) changed this: each view is one Tab stop that lands on a work order, and the arrow keys move between cards, rows, headers and columns. This case follows version 61, the latest.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S3-R13: “Reveal the card’s more-actions overlay on hover or keyboard focus.”
  • S3-R14: “Include Reassign lead technician in the card’s more-actions menu.”
  • S11-R1: “Each view is a single Tab stop. Tab lands on one work order row (Tech View) or card (Board View), the one last focused, or the first one when none has been (never a group or column header while a work order is shown; when every group is collapsed, Tab lands on the first group header; after the user arrows onto a header and tabs out and back in, Tab returns to a work order row while any row is shown; on Board View, if the last-focused card has scrolled out of view in its column, Tab lands on the first card in view); the focused row or card shows a visible focus ring.”
  • S11-R3: “Inside a view the arrow keys move focus: Up and Down move between rows and group headers in Tech View, and between cards and the column header within a Board View column; Left and Right move between Board View columns. Tab from a focused row, card or header reaches its own controls (more actions, pin, collapse) in order, then leaves the view. Tab never stops on every row.”
